note: A SITE, placed. One area bound to one prefab, on the base that builds terrain — and that combination did not exist: a surround rings a DECLARED extent, and until a one-area campaign's single prefab counted as one, `areas[]` had no way to state a map at all. Its remedy was a site plan, which `DW0839` refuses beside a non-empty `areas[]`, so the campaign class that most wants ground around its piece was the one class that could not have it. `gallery-bank` is what a site is: three courses of island mass, a bank of grass across the whole footprint out to the box's own edge, and a walled court on top of it. Two things only a site can ask are asked here. The piece is seated by its WALK PLANE (`VALLEY_WALK_REF_Y`, 64 — the y a body's feet occupy standing on the valley's gap floor), so the origin is 60 and the bank's top course lands exactly on the ground outside it; seated on the old fixed datum it would have stood four courses proud and the party would have met a cliff. And `DW0885` gets both its halves from one piece: of the 1236 solid cells the bank puts on its own box boundary, 852 have nothing in front of them but only 276 stand in air the party can be in — the courses under the bank are inside the valley's own earth — and the parapet above the grade is answered for by four `shown_faces`, all four bound. `up` and `down` are deliberately not among them: the box's top plane is open sky and its underside is buried, and `DW0885` refuses a declared side of pure air exactly as it refuses an undeclared exposed one. The surround here is 10 templates around [0,0]..[23,23] with 1501 standable gap-floor cells, which is the other half of the point: the party can walk OFF the piece, onto ground the horizon built, and the climb proof is what says it cannot get any further than the rim. It carries its own `classes.json`, and the one thing that differs from the primary's is that neither kit holds a `flask`. That is an authored statement rather than a trim: `tools/check-gallery-stageable.py` asks of every build point that each defect class it CONTAINS has a live binding check on it, and a declared recovery kit is what makes the souls rows apply. Inheriting the primary's kits put a flask in a five-minute walk across a walled bank — a flask nothing refills, which is `bell-01` UNBOUND, and it pulls `bell-08`, `bell-04` and `bell-14` behind it as each is answered in turn. This point is not a souls campaign: it has no fire, nothing to rest from and nothing to kill, and the ledger's word for that is INAPPLICABLE — counted and named, never a hole.
